NVDA.what: A director or top executive joined or left
NVDA.short: On November 22, 2026, Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and director, effective immediately. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, stays as CFO. An independent committee's investigation into reports of a foreign intelligence effort targeting Huang will continue.

Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier (up 20% from the prior quarter). It forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, with no China Data Center compute revenue assumed.

AMD.short: On November 18, 2026, AMD's board amended the company's bylaws, effective immediately. The changes add stricter procedures and disclosure rules for stockholder director nominations and proposals, let the company disregard noncompliant nominee votes, require non-white proxy cards, and update the legal forum rules.

short.AMD: These are all opinion pieces, and the few concrete events are thinly sourced. A short-seller report from Hunterbrook alleged heavy China exposure, which AMD denied, citing export-law compliance. Coatue reportedly sold its AMD stake, and the stock rose 6.85% on Nov. 23 as AI chips rebounded. The pieces split between valuation worries and strong growth forecasts.
short.NVDA: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO about 11 days after his resignation, and the stock jumped roughly 31% on Nov. 23, adding nearly $1 trillion in value. It matters because the leadership uncertainty had helped drive a large sell-off. Nearly all the coverage is opinion, and it flags unresolved risks: an SEC accounting probe, China chip-smuggling investigations, and no public succession plan.
short.META: Both recent articles are opinion pieces, so no new company event is reported. Zacks notes Meta fell 40% after its 2012 IPO but is up over 1900% since. The Motley Fool cites 27.5% revenue growth, but also heavy ad dependence, legal risks including a $25B New Mexico penalty, and negative free cash flow from AI spending.
